guide.summary: UBS scans JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, C/C++, Rust, Go, Java/Kotlin, Ruby, Swift, C# and Elixir for likely bugs and security issues. Run it on the files you just changed, read the machine-readable envelope, fix criticals, re-run until exit 0.
guide.golden_rule: ubs <changed-files> --format=json before every commit; exit 0 = safe, 1 = findings, 2 = environment/partial/refused, 3 = nothing scanned.
guide.stdout_contract: In --format=json|jsonl|sarif|toon mode stdout is exactly one machine-readable document (or one JSONL stream); every diagnostic goes to stderr.
workflow: Scope the scan to changed files: ubs a.ts b.py --format=json (sub-second) rather than the whole tree.

Read totals.critical / totals.warning and status; status=partial means a module timed out, crashed, or reported itself partial (the Rust module when cargo could not run) and exit is 2 unless UBS_ALLOW_PARTIAL=1.
Findings live under scanners[].findings[] with severity, count, title, description and samples[{file,line,code}].
Suppress a confirmed false positive with a trailing `ubs:ignore` comment (or the line above); never delete the check.
Re-run the same command until exit 0, then commit.

subcommands.name: scan
subcommands.description: Default. Scans the project directory or the listed files/directories (union scan).

subcommands.name: doctor
subcommands.description: Verify cached modules/helpers and the ast-grep toolchain; --fix re-downloads corrupted copies; --format=json emits structured checks.

subcommands.name: explain
subcommands.description: Explain a rule: message, remediation, fixture examples, confidence, category.

subcommands.name: --schema
subcommands.description: JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for each output format.

flags.name: --format
flags.description: Output format: text (default), json, jsonl, sarif, toon.

flags.name: --output
flags.description: Also write the report to FILE (alias: -o FILE, or a trailing positional file that does not exist yet); stdout still receives it.

flags.name: --ci
flags.description: CI mode: stable UTC timestamps; also disables the auto-update check.

flags.name: --fail-on-warning
flags.description: Exit 1 when warnings exist, not only criticals.

flags.name: --only
flags.description: Restrict to these languages (js, python, c/cpp, rust, golang, java, kotlin/kt, ruby, swift, csharp/cs, elixir/ex, bash/sh).

flags.name: --exclude-langs
flags.description: Skip these languages.

flags.name: --exclude
flags.description: Skip paths (globs/dirs with .ubsignore semantics); forwarded to every module. A bare language name with no such path is rejected (use --exclude-langs).

flags.name: --include-ext
flags.description: Extra file extensions forwarded to the language modules.

flags.name: --rules
flags.description: Directory of custom ast-grep YAML rules (or an ast-grep project, whose sgconfig ruleDirs are loaded) that every language module runs. Repeatable; a rule id defined by two files refuses the scan (duplicate-rule-id).

flags.name: --skip
flags.description: Skip categories by stable id (e.g. python.todo) or category number.

flags.name: --skip-LANG
flags.description: Skip categories in one language (LANG = js|python|cpp|rust|golang|java|kotlin|ruby|swift|csharp|elixir|bash).

flags.name: --category
flags.description: Focus on a category pack (currently resource-lifecycle).

flags.name: --profile
flags.description: Severity profile passed to the modules (strict|loose); strict also implies --fail-on-warning.

flags.name: --files
flags.description: Scan only the listed files (comma or space separated).

flags.name: --staged
flags.description: Scan only files staged in the git index.

flags.name: --diff
flags.description: Scan only files modified in the working tree (alias --git-diff).

flags.name: --list-categories
flags.description: Print each selected module's category numbers/names and exit 0.

flags.name: --jobs
flags.description: Parallelism hint passed to modules that support it.

flags.name: --ignore-file
flags.description: Extra ignore globs (default: PROJECT/.ubsignore when present).

flags.name: --skip-size-check
flags.description: Skip the directory size guard (default limit 1000 MB after ignores).

flags.name: --skip-type-narrowing
flags.description: Skip the JS/Rust/Kotlin/Swift/C# type-narrowing helpers.

flags.name: --no-cargo
flags.description: Rust static-only mode: skip every cargo phase (fmt/clippy, check/test --no-run, audit/deny/udeps/outdated). Skipped categories report a 'Not evaluated' finding and the Rust JSON carries meta.cargo_execution.status=skipped. Env equivalent: UBS_SKIP_RUST_BUILD=1.

flags.name: --go-tools
flags.description: Run optional read-only gofmt, go vet and govulncheck; fresh findings and coverage status reach all formats.

flags.name: --test-pkgs
flags.description: Go package patterns per selected module, parsed as arguments without shell evaluation.

flags.name: --go-timeout
flags.description: Execution timeout for each optional Go analyzer invocation.

flags.name: --module-dir
flags.description: Where modules and helpers are cached.

flags.name: --update-modules
flags.description: Re-download modules before scanning.

flags.name: --comparison
flags.description: Baseline JSON to annotate the shareable report with deltas (exit code still reflects current totals).

flags.name: --baseline
flags.description: Baseline JSON file for comparison or diff mode (alias for --comparison).

flags.name: --save-baseline
flags.description: Save the current scan findings and totals to FILE as a baseline.

flags.name: --new-only
flags.description: Report only findings not present in the baseline (diff mode).

flags.name: --report-json
flags.description: Write the combined summary JSON to FILE.

flags.name: --html-report
flags.description: Write a shareable HTML report.

flags.name: --beads-jsonl
flags.description: Write findings as JSONL for Beads/strung.

flags.name: --jsonl-summary-only
flags.description: JSONL: emit only scanner/totals lines, no per-finding lines.

flags.name: --suggest-ignore
flags.description: Print large-directory ignore suggestions without modifying files.

flags.name: --no-color
flags.description: Disable ANSI colors (same as NO_COLOR=1).

flags.name: --verbose
flags.description: More code samples per finding (alias -v).

flags.name: --quiet
flags.description: Less console output (alias -q).

flags.name: --no-auto-update
flags.description: Disable the opt-in auto-update check.

flags.name: --no-cache
flags.description: Disable reading and writing the Merkle-keyed scan cache.

flags.name: --cache-dir
flags.description: Directory for scan cache (default: $XDG_CACHE_HOME/ubs or ~/.cache/ubs).

flags.name: --update
flags.description: Update the installed ubs from the latest verified release and exit.

flags.name: --version
flags.description: Print the version and exit 0.

flags.name: --help
flags.description: Human help text (alias -h).

examples.goal: Skip a directory for this run
Accept a partial run (a module timed out)
Explain a rule with remediation and fixture examples
Validate an output against its schema

exit_codes.meaning: No critical findings (no warnings either with --fail-on-warning); every requested language was scanned.

Invalid arguments, environment error (e.g. ast-grep missing, module failed verification), refused scan (directory too large, $HOME, /), or a partial run (module timeout/crash) unless UBS_ALLOW_PARTIAL=1. Machine formats still print an envelope on stdout.
Nothing was scanned: no supported language detected. Not a pass; UBS_ALLOW_NO_SCAN=1 restores exit 0.

json.description: One object: project, timestamp, status (ok|partial), failed_modules[], scanners[] (per-language summary with findings[] and status ok|timeout|error), totals{critical,warning,info,files}. Environment errors and refusals print an error envelope instead; no supported language prints a result object with exit_code 3.

jsonl.description: One JSON object per line: type=finding (per finding, with language), type=scanner (per language summary), type=totals (last line, carries status/failed_modules), or type=error (envelope).

sarif.description: SARIF 2.1.0; one run per module. Partial runs and errors set runs[].invocations[0].executionSuccessful=false with toolExecutionNotifications (descriptor ids ubs/module-timeout, ubs/module-error, ubs/<refusal-or-error-reason>).

toon.description: The json document encoded with toon_rust's tru. Without a usable toon_rust encoder (toon or tru on PATH, TOON_TRU_BIN/TOON_BIN, or the tool cache filled by 'ubs doctor --fix'/install.sh) the run exits 2 with the error envelope (reason toon-encoder-missing) instead of printing JSON labelled as TOON.

text.description: Human report; Combined Summary at the end (Files/Critical/Warning/Info, Status: partial when applicable).

env.name: UBS_MODULE_TIMEOUT
env.description: Override automatic per-module timeout (3x estimated cost, minimum 300s); 0 disables.

env.name: UBS_ALLOW_PARTIAL
env.description: Exit on findings even when a module timed out or crashed (envelope still says partial).

env.name: UBS_PROFILE
env.description: Add a profile block (total_ms, list_ms, fanout_ms, merge_ms, modules{lang: ms}) to json/toon output and a Profile line to the text summary.

env.name: UBS_ALLOW_NO_SCAN
env.description: Exit 0 instead of 3 when no supported language is detected.

env.name: UBS_MAX_DIR_SIZE_MB
env.description: Refuse to scan directories larger than N MB after ignores (default 1000; 0 disables). Measured over the listed files: binary/media/archive/data files and files above UBS_MAX_FILE_MB are not counted or copied.

env.name: UBS_MAX_FILE_MB
env.description: Leave files above N MB out of whole-project scans (default 8; 0 disables).

env.name: UBS_PYTHON
env.description: Python >= 3.9 interpreter to expose as python3 for the run (a python/py -3 on PATH is used automatically when python3 is missing).

env.name: UBS_ENABLE_AUTO_UPDATE
env.description: Opt in to the 24h auto-update check.

env.name: UBS_RULES
env.description: Custom rule directories (':'-separated, like PATH) used when no --rules is given; empty entries are ignored.

env.name: UBS_CACHE_DIR
env.description: Override root directory for scan cache (like --cache-dir).
